title: The Bomb That Bounced Across Water to Break a Dam

scenes.text: In 1943, Britain made a bomb that bounced across water.
Bombers flew just sixty feet above the lake at about 240 miles an hour.
The bomb was spun at five hundred turns a minute, then dropped.
It skipped over the surface like a stone, and the backspin made it hug the dam wall.
Two dams broke, and the flood rushed through the valley.
A bomb that skipped like a stone.

description:
On the night of May sixteenth, 1943, nineteen Lancaster bombers attacked German dams with a spinning bouncing bomb.
They flew sixty feet above the water at about 240 miles an hour, and two dams were breached.
It was one of the most daring raids of the war.
thumbnail_text: THE BOMB THAT SKIPPED LIKE A STONE
first_comment: The bomb was spun at 500 rpm to make it bounce. What other WW2 invention surprises you?
